hook: *94.78 lakh* vehicles and counting: a study floats paying to drive
hook_b: *94.78 lakh* vehicles and counting: a study floats paying to drive
tldr: A BITS Pilani-led study says congestion pricing on Hyderabad's busiest corridors, plus better public transport, could ease traffic as vehicles near one crore.

beats.what: Researchers from BITS Pilani Hyderabad, Cardiff University and KFUPM surveyed 435 car commuters and suggest charging motorists on the most congested corridors at peak hours.
beats.why: Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri had 94.78 lakh registered vehicles in 2025, up from 89.89 lakh in 2024, and road widening has not kept pace.
beats.care: If you drive to the IT corridor, experts name it as the most suitable place to pilot congestion charges or carpool lanes.

causes.label: Vehicles rose 89.89 to 94.78 lakh in a year

effects.label: IT corridor suggested for a pilot
Fees could fund buses and footpaths

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Researchers say charge revenue could fund buses, feeder networks and footpaths; commuters were willing to pay if it cut travel time.

cards.q: Should cars pay a fee to use Hyderabad's busiest roads at peak hours?

qs: Would a road charge move commuters to Metro and buses, or onto side roads?
Who would decide which corridors get priced?

facts.t: HITEC City main road carries an estimated *1.5 lakh* vehicles a day.
The study surveyed *435* car commuters; faster travel was the top benefit they expected.

viz.verdict: More vehicles on the same roads, slower trips for commuters

viz.l: Single-occupancy vehicles per hour at Cyber Towers
viz.verdict: Most cars on the stretch carry one person, the study's carpool case

learn.t: Congestion pricing = a fee to drive on busy roads or zones at peak hours

watch: No government decision is reported; experts suggest a pilot on the IT corridor and HOV lanes for shared cars.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: One Crore Vehicles On Horizon, Should Hyderabad Put Price on Gridlock?
